apiContracts: No API route or server-side authorization contract changes.
The existing reader progress API, bookmark API and chapter unlock API retain their canonical request/ownership behavior.
dataEntities: No new database entity, column or migration. Existing imperial_language localStorage preference remains canonical.

migrationPlan.canonicalEntityReuse: Reuses the browser-local imperial_language preference and the existing IN_LANG dictionary.
migrationPlan.backwardCompatibility: Existing language preference remains valid; English remains the fallback when a translation key is unavailable.
migrationPlan.rollbackOrForwardRepair: Revert the selector, locale dictionary and reader text wrappers; no data repair is needed.

uiLifecycle.clientBootBehavior: Settings restores the existing language preference, and the reader resolves static/dynamic labels from the active fourteen-locale dictionary.

privacySecurity.ownerScoping: Reader progress, bookmarks and unlocks remain session-owned; no owner identifiers are introduced by localization.
privacySecurity.rateAndSizeLimits: No API input or rate limits change.
privacySecurity.rightsAndPrivacy: Creator-authored chapter content is not translated or rewritten.

unit: Existing reader progress, bookmark and unlock regressions.
test-reader-accessibility.mjs: initial and live progress announcements use the active locale without losing progressbar semantics.
integration: Settings language selection restores and updates the shared interface locale; reader progress/footer labels and locked-chapter copy use the selected locale.
isolation: Creator-authored chapter text and account-owned reading state remain untouched.

stagingSteps: Run all six exact-head architecture, source, route, schema, migration and Graphify workflows.
Verify settings language restore and live switch across fourteen locales.
Verify reader locked chapter, progress and footer labels across Urdu, Arabic and Persian as well as LTR locales.
Verify source and versioned browser bundle parity.

rollback.codeRollback: Revert the settings selector, locale dictionary, readerText helper, marked labels and tests together.
rollback.dataRollbackOrForwardRepair: No persistent data or database change.
monitoringSignals: Existing reader progress and bookmark regressions

collisionReview.duplicateRoutes: No new route; existing settings and reader routes reused.
collisionReview.sharedSurfaceOwners: Experience shell owns settings and language selection; reader experience owns reader labels; platform quality owns tests; architecture owns contract.

changeSummary: Adds a fourteen-locale settings language selector and ten reader strings on the canonical 17.23 runtime while preserving account preferences, progress synchronization, bookmarks, unlocks and six-theme reading. Keeps the existing reader accessibility regression aligned with translated progress value text. Applies the active locale after reader markup handoff so static chapter labels, bookmark controls and reader-theme accessibility names are translated.
acceptanceCriteria: The existing settings page offers a native-language selector for all fourteen supported locales.
Saved imperial_language is restored when settings opens and changes immediately through setINLang.
Ten reader strings exist in all fourteen locales and dynamic progress/footer labels use readerText.
Locked-chapter explanation and Imperial Crowns label are translatable.
Existing reader progress, bookmark, unlock, library and account-preference behaviors remain unchanged.
Canonical and served 17.23 browser bundles are byte-identical.
No API route, database entity, migration, production data mutation or deployment is introduced.
Initial and live reader progress announcements use the active locale while retaining labeled progressbar semantics.
Reader markup applies the active locale after rendering; bookmark and reader-theme accessible names follow the selected language.
